_read_me: Every number the planner uses that is not typed in by the family lives here. Each entry has value, unit, source and as_of. A value of null with source TODO means it has not been checked yet; the app shows 'not set yet' instead of guessing. Values filled on 2026-10-02 were found by Claude from the sources listed and still need Sahas to double-check.

default_interest_rate.source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, 30-year fixed average: https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-average-728
default_interest_rate.note: National weekly average. A family's real rate depends on credit, points and lender, so they can type their own. Update weekly or before the video.

default_term_years.source: Matches the loan the rate above is for (Freddie Mac surveys the 30-year fixed)

minimum_down_payment_percent.source: My Home by Freddie Mac, 'Unlock Homeownership with Just 3% Down': Home Possible 'provides down payment options as low as 3%': https://myhome.freddiemac.com/buying/3-percent-down-payment
minimum_down_payment_percent.note: The lowest down payment the planner allows. Many loans need more; some programs (FHA, VA) differ.

estimate_to_sale_price_ratio.unit: model estimate divided by sale price (median)
estimate_to_sale_price_ratio.source: This project's sales check (housing_model_v2.ipynb, saved in data/summary.json under alpharetta_sales_check, 2025): 308 Alpharetta homes sold in 2025, and the model's estimate was a median 0.78 of the sale price (county values were 0.786).
estimate_to_sale_price_ratio.note: Measured in Alpharetta (Fulton County), not Forsyth: Forsyth has no open sale records yet. The planner divides each estimate by this to get a likely sale price (about 28% higher), so homes are not judged as cheaper than they sell for. Replace with a Forsyth number once the Board of Assessors sales records arrive.

assessment_ratio.source: Georgia Department of Revenue, Property Tax Valuation (O.C.G.A. § 48-5-7): https://dor.georgia.gov/property-tax-valuation
assessment_ratio.note: Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value unless the law says otherwise.

forsyth_county.source: Forsyth County, 'Forsyth County Commission Adopts Millage Rates' (Aug 8, 2025): county 7.896 (M&O 4.791 + fire 2.805 + bond 0.300) + schools 16.626 (M&O 15.208 + bonds 1.418): https://www.forsythco.com/news/2025/08/forsyth-county-commission-adopts-millage-rates-2025/
forsyth_county.note: Unincorporated Forsyth. City of Cumming homes pay a city rate on top, which the data can't tell apart. For 2026 the county lowered its M&O rate to 4.727 (forsythco.com, Aug 2026); update once the 2026 school rate is confirmed on an official page.

homestead_exemption.note: Not applied yet, so tax estimates run a little high for a primary residence. Rules differ by county and need an official source.

homeowners_rate_per_1000.unit: dollars per year per $1,000 of home value
homeowners_rate_per_1000.source: Freddie Mac Research, 'The Cost of Homeowners' Insurance' (Mar 20, 2024), 2023 national average for Freddie Mac borrowers: https://www.freddiemac.com/research/insight/homeowners-insurance-costs
homeowners_rate_per_1000.note: National, not Georgia, and premiums have risen since 2023. The home page lets a family type in a real quote instead.

monthly_per_100k.source: My Home by Freddie Mac, 'Breaking down PMI': 'approximately between $30 and $70 per month for every $100,000 borrowed': https://myhome.freddiemac.com/buying/breaking-down-pmi
monthly_per_100k.note: Uses the high end of Freddie Mac's range so the plan doesn't come up short. Real cost depends on credit score and down payment.

required_below_down_payment_percent.source: My Home by Freddie Mac, 'Breaking down PMI': required 'if you make a down payment less than 20%': https://myhome.freddiemac.com/buying/breaking-down-pmi
required_below_down_payment_percent.note: Mortgage insurance is added when the down payment is under this.

percent_of_price.source: CFPB, 'Determine your down payment': 'closing costs (not including your down payment) range from 2-5% of the home purchase price': https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/prepare/determine-your-down-payment/
percent_of_price.note: Uses the high end of the CFPB range so the plan doesn't come up short. The same CFPB page says to subtract closing costs from your cash to get your down payment, which is how the planner does it.

housing_share_of_gross_income.source: CFPB 'Buying a house: monthly payment worksheet': 'A mortgage lending rule of thumb is that your total monthly housing obligations should be no more than 28% of your pre-tax income': https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/cfpb_buying-a-house_monthly-payment_worksheet.pdf
housing_share_of_gross_income.note: Shown only as a reference line, never as a rule.

comfortable_min_left_percent.unit: percent of take-home pay left after all monthly costs
comfortable_min_left_percent.source: Sahas's v3 spec draft (family_home_buying_planner_v3_specification.md, section 6). DESIGN.md section 7 says the cutoffs still need to be justified before launch.
comfortable_min_left_percent.note: At or above this share left = Comfortable. PLACEHOLDER: Sahas to confirm or change.
comfortable_min_left_percent.cite: placeholder from the v3 spec draft

stretching_below_left_percent.unit: percent of take-home pay left after all monthly costs
stretching_below_left_percent.source: Sahas's v3 spec draft (family_home_buying_planner_v3_specification.md, section 6). DESIGN.md section 7 says the cutoffs still need to be justified before launch.
stretching_below_left_percent.note: Below this share left = Stretching. Between the two = Tight. PLACEHOLDER: Sahas to confirm or change.
stretching_below_left_percent.cite: placeholder from the v3 spec draft
